components.title: Button
components.purpose:
Starts an action on the current screen: submit, save, open, delete. One primary button per region of
a screen; everything else is a quieter variant. Navigation to another page is a link, not a button.
anatomy: Container — the `<button>` (or the child element with `asChild`), height and radius from the size and the brand recipe.
Leading or trailing icon — optional SVG, sized automatically per size.
Label — a verb and an object, one to three words.

variants.use: The one main action in a region: Save, Place order.
Strong emphasis that should not use the key colour, for example on a brand-coloured surface.
The alternative beside a primary: Close next to Confirm.
A bordered secondary action in toolbars and dense forms.
Low-emphasis actions in dense UI, and icon-only buttons.
A key-colour text action without a surface: Retry, Maybe later.
An action that deletes or cannot be undone.

sizes.use: Inline secondary actions; matches the default input and select height.
Large or full-width CTA, including a CTA fixed to the bottom of a mobile screen.
Icon-only button, for example in a top bar. Needs an `aria-label`.

states.note: Keep the label readable; explain why nearby if it is not obvious.

states.looks: 2px ring in the brand colour at 20%.

states.note: Swap the label for a 16px spinner, keep the size, block clicks (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §46).

do: Label the outcome: "Save changes", "Delete project", never "Submit" or "OK" (UX-WRITING WB-1, WB-2).
In a pair, put the primary on the right and the secondary on the left, 12px apart (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §46).
Name both outcomes in a destructive dialog: "Delete / Keep" (UX-WRITING WB-3).
Give icon-only buttons an `aria-label`.
dont: Don't put two primary buttons in one region.
Don't shrink on press (`active:scale`) or use a gradient background (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §46).
Don't recolour a variant through `className` (`bg-…`); pick a variant or add one to the contract.
Don't use `destructive` for emphasis that is not destructive.
knownGaps: DESIGN-LANGUAGE §46 still lists hex values for `neutral` (#2A2A2A) and `secondary` (#F3F4F5) and a fixed radius per size (xs pill, sm/md 10px, lg 14px). The code uses theme roles (`foreground`, `secondary`) and one recipe control radius for every size. The code is the current contract; §46 is stale.
`md` (40px), `sm` (36px), `xs` (32px) and `icon` (40px) are under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41).

The default `md` button (40px) is taller than the default input and select (36px), so the defaults break "buttons, inputs and selects in one context share a height" (CRAFT-BASELINE). Use `sm` beside default form controls.
There is no hover style; pointer users get feedback only on press.
There is no loading state; §46 describes one.
sources: DESIGN-LANGUAGE §46 Button design rules; §41 Touch targets; §24 Interaction rules

code.radius: recipe control radius (`ss-pattern-control` → `--ss-control-radius`, 0–999px by brand recipe)
flags: Height under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41): `xs` 32px, `sm` 36px, `md` 40px, `icon` 40px. On touch surfaces, extend the hit area or use a taller size.

components.title: Badge
components.purpose:
A short, static label for a status, a category or a count. It informs; it does not act. For a
selectable chip or filter use `Toggle` (or a `Button` at size `xs`); there is no separate chip component.
anatomy: Container — a `<span>` (or the child element with `asChild`, for example a link).
Optional icon — 12px SVG before the text.
Text — one to three words.

variants.use: The one label that should stand out in a group.
Quiet labels in dense tables and lists.

states.looks: Background at 90% when rendered as a link (`asChild` with `<a>`).
3px ring in the `ring` role at 50%, border in `ring`.

states.note: Rare; inherited from the form styles.

do: Pair colour with text or an icon; never let colour alone carry the status (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41).
Keep the text short and in one form across the product ("Paid", not "Payment completed" in one place and "Paid" in another).
Use `secondary` by default and save `default` for the one label that matters.
dont: Don't attach a click handler to a badge; use `Toggle` or `Button`.
Don't use `destructive` for a status that is not an error.
Don't invent a colour per category through `className`; categories that need colour need tokens.
knownGaps: Badge uses the `primary` and `secondary` roles while Button's primary uses `brand`. In a skin where `primary` and `brand` differ, a default badge and a primary button do not match.
The radius is a fixed `rounded-md`, not the recipe control radius that Button and Tabs use.
The theme has `success`, `warning` and `info` roles but Badge has no variants for them; DESIGN-LANGUAGE §11 gives urgent and info badge colours as hex (#C85A54, #7A7A7A) instead of roles.
Link hover darkens by opacity (`/90`), which DESIGN-LANGUAGE §46 rejects for buttons.
sources: DESIGN-LANGUAGE §11 Badge color rules; §41 Accessibility (colour not alone); §46 Button design rules

components.title: Tabs
components.purpose:
Switches between views of the same content in place, without leaving the page: Overview / Activity,
Week / Month. Each tab shows a panel; only one panel is visible at a time.
anatomy: `Tabs` — the root that holds the selected value.
`TabsList` — the track that holds the triggers.
`TabsTrigger` — one tab; the selected one sits on a card-coloured surface.
`TabsContent` — the panel for one tab.

states.note: Say why elsewhere if the reason is not obvious.

do: Use two to five tabs with short labels.
Switch instantly; no slide animation between panels (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §42).
Keep each panel about the same kind of content so switching compares like with like.
dont: Don't use tabs for steps in a sequence (use a stepper) or to move between pages (use links).
Don't nest tabs inside tabs.
Don't hide information the user needs to compare at a glance behind separate tabs; show it side by side.
knownGaps: The track is 36px tall, under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41).
Only the segmented style exists. The token canon sample (`research/tokens`, `component.tab.bd.active`) assumes an underline tab with an active border; there is no underline variant yet.
For two to four options inside a card header, DESIGN-LANGUAGE §10 asks for a pill toggle; `SegmentedControl` or `ToggleGroup` fits that job better than Tabs.
sources: DESIGN-LANGUAGE §42 Tab & navigation details; §10 Selection UI rules; §41 Touch targets

code.radius: recipe control radius (`ss-pattern-control` → `--ss-control-radius`, 0–999px by brand recipe)
flags: Height under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41): `tabs-list` 36px. On touch surfaces, extend the hit area or use a taller size.

components.title: Input
components.purpose:
Single-line text entry: a name, an email, an amount, a search term. Pair it with a visible label;
multi-line text uses `Textarea`.
anatomy: Label — a separate `Label` above the field, linked with `htmlFor` / `id`.
Field — the `<input>`.
Help or error text — a separate element below, linked with `aria-describedby`.

states.note: Set `aria-invalid` and show the message below the field.

do: Put the label above the field (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §44).
Validate on blur, and for Korean, Japanese or Chinese input only after `compositionend` (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §44).
Say what happened and how to fix it next to the field (UX-WRITING WE-1, WE-2).
Keep 16px text on phones so iOS does not zoom on focus; the component does this below the `md` breakpoint.
dont: Don't use the placeholder as the label.
Don't validate while the user is still typing.
Don't put inputs inside consumer-service cards; use a separate page or bottom sheet (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §44, consumer-service scope).
knownGaps: DESIGN-LANGUAGE §44 specifies a 48px field (`h-12`), `rounded-xl`, a transparent border and a brand-coloured focus ring. The code is 36px (`h-9`), `rounded-md`, an `input` border and a `ring`-coloured focus ring. The two disagree; the code is what ships until the designer decides (#96).
36px is under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41).
The radius is a fixed `rounded-md`, not the recipe control radius, so an input and a button side by side can have different corners.
sources: DESIGN-LANGUAGE §44 Input & form rules; §41 Touch targets

flags: Height under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41): `input` 36px. On touch surfaces, extend the hit area or use a taller size.
Radius is fixed (rounded-md) instead of the recipe control radius used by Button and Tabs.

components.title: Select
components.purpose:
Chooses one option from a list that is too long to show at once (five or more). For two to four
options, show them all with a segmented control or radio group.
anatomy: `Select` — the root that holds the value.
`SelectTrigger` — the field that shows `SelectValue` and a chevron.
`SelectContent` — the popover list, with scroll buttons when it overflows.
`SelectItem` — one option; the chosen one shows a check.
`SelectGroup`, `SelectLabel`, `SelectSeparator` — optional grouping.

sizes.use: Forms and settings; matches the default input height.

do: Use it for five or more options; a native `<select>` is also fine in settings and forms (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §10).
Give it a visible label, like an input.
Order options meaningfully: by frequency, alphabetically, or in their natural order.
dont: Don't use a select for two to four options inside a consumer-service card; use a pill toggle (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §10).
Don't use it for actions; a menu of actions is a `DropdownMenu`.
knownGaps: The trigger is 36px (`default`) or 32px (`sm`), under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41).
The trigger's radius is set by its own classes, not the recipe control radius used by Button and Tabs.
sources: DESIGN-LANGUAGE §10 Selection UI rules; §41 Touch targets

flags: Height under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41): `select-trigger` size `default` 36px, `select-trigger` size `sm` 32px. On touch surfaces, extend the hit area or use a taller size.
Radius is fixed (rounded-md, rounded-sm) instead of the recipe control radius used by Button and Tabs.

components.title: Switch
components.purpose:
Turns one setting on or off, and the change applies immediately: notifications, dark mode,
auto-renew. A choice that only applies after Save is a `Checkbox`.
anatomy: Track — the `Switch` root; filled with `primary` when on.
Thumb — the circle that moves right when on.
Label — a separate `Label` next to it, linked with `htmlFor` / `id`.
do: Always pair it with a visible label that names the setting, not the action ("Email notifications", not "Turn on").
Apply the change immediately and show the result.
Make the label clickable too, so the whole row is a target.
dont: Don't use a switch inside a form that needs a submit; use a checkbox.
Don't use a switch without a label, or with a label that changes between on and off.
knownGaps: The track is about 18px × 32px, far under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41). Make the label and row the target, or wrap the switch in a 44px area.

The track uses `transition-all`. DESIGN-LANGUAGE §24 recommends `transition-all` for interactive elements, while the rule catalog's detector SS003 asks for named properties. The two documents disagree.
On uses `primary`, not `brand`, so it may not match a primary button in skins where the two roles differ.

flags: Height under the 44px touch minimum (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §41): `switch` 18.4px × 32px. On touch surfaces, extend the hit area or use a taller size.
Uses `transition-all`; name the transitioned properties (detector SS003).
Radius is fixed (rounded-full) instead of the recipe control radius used by Button and Tabs.

components.title: Table
components.purpose:
Compares records across the same columns: orders, invoices, team members. Use a table when people
scan down a column or across a row to compare; use a list when each item is read on its own.
anatomy: `Table` — a horizontally scrollable container and the `<table>`.
`TableHeader`, `TableBody`, `TableFooter` — row groups.
`TableRow` — one record.
`TableHead` — a column header cell.
`TableCell` — a data cell.
`TableCaption` — the table's title or summary, below the table.
do: Give every table a caption or an `aria-label`.
Right-align numbers and use tabular figures (`text-right tabular-nums`) so digits line up (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §22).
Keep one unit per column and say it in the header.
dont: Don't use a table for layout.
Don't put interactive controls in every cell; give the row one clear action.
Don't highlight rows on hover in consumer-service screens, where DESIGN-LANGUAGE §24 forbids hover highlights on list rows.
knownGaps: There is no numeric-column helper; every consumer adds `text-right tabular-nums` by hand.
Row hover is always on, which conflicts with DESIGN-LANGUAGE §24 in the consumer-service recipe.
All cells use `whitespace-nowrap`, so long text forces horizontal scrolling on phones.
